goal.text: Yeah is an Emacs Lisp agent harness: the harness runs in a dedicated Emacs process (the service placement); the model goes through gptel, every tool goes through the registry and the permission system, the session log stays append-only, and the editor reaches it through the bridge or an ACP/MCP client

claims.text: every file under lib/ byte-compiles without errors and without warnings
claims.falsifier: the byte-compilation of lib/ fails or reports a warning

claims.text: all ERT unit tests pass
claims.falsifier: an ERT unit test fails

claims.text: a session/cancel on the socket transport stops a running prompt
claims.falsifier: a cancel that arrives during a running prompt is read only after the prompt settles
claims.control: sed -i 's/(yeah-turn-cancel turn "cancelled by ACP client")/(progn)/' lib/yeah-acp.el

claims.text: the emacsclient bridge reads and edits the live buffers of a real Emacs server
claims.falsifier: the bridge is checked only against a stub, or a live read returns the wrong text

claims.text: two sessions in one Emacs run at once without cross-talk, and cancelling one leaves the other
claims.falsifier: an event of one run lands in the journal of the other

claims.text: the ACP and MCP servers answer over stdio with the real protocol
claims.falsifier: a stdio server does not answer or answers with the wrong protocol

claims.text: a 10 MiB token estimate does not block the event loop beyond a 100 ms timer
claims.falsifier: the estimate walks the text character by character and the timer fires seconds late

claims.text: the package entry declares the supported Emacs and gptel versions, and the bootstrap installs from lib/ with a pinned gptel
claims.falsifier: the package loses its version declaration or the bootstrap its lib layout

claims.text: a run starts from a snapshot of the registry; a tool one run registers is not advertised to another run or the shared registry
claims.falsifier: a tool one run registers appears in the shared registry or in another run
claims.control: sed -i 's|(puthash name spec (yeah-tools--active-registry))|(puthash name spec yeah-tools--registry)|' lib/yeah-tools.el

claims.text: a service Emacs starts, serves a prompt over the socket, writes the turn to its journal and stops
claims.falsifier: the service does not answer, or the journal has no turn

claims.text: the editor client connects to a service Emacs and drives a prompt over the socket, seeing the streamed updates
claims.falsifier: the client cannot connect, or the prompt is not answered, or no update arrives

claims.text: M-x yeah-service opens a buffer that drives a service Emacs: the question, the streamed answer and the stop reason are rendered
claims.falsifier: the buffer does not show the question, the answer or the stop reason

claims.text: an answer that only announces the next step, or a result no tool backs, is nudged into the action; a result that a tool backs ends the run
claims.falsifier: the run ends without acting, or a run that acted is nudged anyway
claims.control: sed -i 's|(and (< (yeah-turn-nudges turn) (yeah-turn-max-nudges turn))|(and nil (< (yeah-turn-nudges turn) (yeah-turn-max-nudges turn))|' lib/yeah-turn.el

claims.text: an answer that arrives while the harness waits for a tool waits for the tools and ends the run instead of failing it
claims.falsifier: the run fails with no transition from awaiting-tool on stream-end
claims.control: sed -i 's|(setf (yeah-turn-pending-answer turn) answer)|(progn (yeah-turn--fail turn "late answer dropped") nil)|' lib/yeah-turn.el

claims.text: the standing permissions the person grants a service reach it: a tool the rules allow is allowed there, and a tool they do not name is asked of the client over the wire
claims.falsifier: the service denies a tool the person granted, or allows — without asking the client — a tool nobody granted

claims.text: a tool that registers another tool while it runs lands in the registry of the run, not in the shared one; the async-continuation path is documented, not silently wrong
claims.falsifier: a tool a run registers while it runs appears in the shared registry

claims.text: with supervision, the model ends the run by calling the finish tool; a text answer alone is not a completion
claims.falsifier: a run completes on a text answer alone when supervision is on

claims.text: the descriptions of the built-in tools are unambiguous: read reads a file from disk by its path, buffer-read reads the content of a live Emacs buffer by its buffer name, every tool names the thing it works on, and no two tools share one description
claims.falsifier: read and buffer-read describe themselves the same way, or a tool description names another tool's subject, or two tools share one description
claims.control: sed -i 's|:description "Read the content of a live Emacs buffer.*"|:description "Read a file from disk by its path, from a 1-based line offset, up to a line limit. Use it for source code and for any file stored on disk."|' lib/yeah-emacs.el

claims.text: the task list of a run is a projection of its journal: the tools todo_add, todo_update and todo_list change the list through todo events of the session log, and a restart that reads the log again finds the same list
claims.falsifier: the task list is not the projection of the journal: the tools do not write the tasks into the log of the run, a restart that reads the log again does not restore the list, or the list survives the loss of its events

claims.text: the git tools show the status and the difference of a project, and write a commit only when the rules allow it
claims.falsifier: the status or the difference does not show the change, or a commit is written although no rule allows it
claims.control: sed -i 's|(user-error "the rules do not allow a commit|(message "the rules do not allow a commit|' lib/yeah-git.el

claims.text: a read of a file open in a buffer gives the model the modification tick it needs for a guarded edit
claims.falsifier: the model's view of a read has no tick

claims.text: the service asks the client before an effect the rules do not name
claims.falsifier: the tool runs although the client refused, or is denied although the client allowed

claims.text: the editor answers the service's permission request over the wire
claims.falsifier: the person's answer never reaches the service, or the question does not name the tool and its target
claims.control: sed -i 's|((and method id)|((and nil method id)|' lib/yeah-client.el

claims.text: the service socket lives where only this user can reach it
claims.falsifier: the socket sits bare in a world-writable directory, so any local user can drive the agent

claims.text: the client notices when the service is gone
claims.falsifier: the person types into a buffer nobody answers: the death of the service is not shown

claims.text: a clean service takes its model from the init file alone
claims.falsifier: the clean service has no model: the init file it loaded is ignored
